title: K-th smallest in a search tree
prompt:
Ticket numbers are stored in a binary search tree with distinct values; return the k-th smallest ticket number (k = 1 means the smallest).

- Nodes have val, left and right (child node or null). In Python they are dicts: node["left"].
- The tree is a valid search tree: smaller values to the left, larger to the right, no duplicates.
- 1 to 10,000 nodes; depth at most 500; values are integers between -10^9 and 10^9; 1 <= k <= number of nodes.
- Return the value (an integer).
hints: Which traversal order lists the values of a search tree in ascending order?
An in-order traversal (left, node, right) visits values from smallest to largest, so the k-th visited node is the answer.
Do the in-order walk iteratively: push the whole left spine onto a stack, pop a node, count it, then move to its right child. Stop the moment the count reaches k.

solution.explanation: In-order traversal of a search tree yields values in sorted order. The iterative version stops after the k-th pop, so it only does the work needed to reach the answer instead of collecting and sorting all n values.

complexity.notes: h is the tree height. Collecting all values and sorting would be O(n log n).

followUps: If the tree is updated often and queried often, what extra field per node would make each query O(h)?
